messages:
Paula Mendes: pushing a quick UX/copy review thread for the incident update templates (Investigating/Identified/Mitigating/Monitoring/Resolved). current draft is in DES-245 + the doc. biggest open question: how transparent can we be in the first 10–15 min when we *don’t know* yet?

Marissa Cole: thanks. +1, we’ve been too confident early and then had to walk things back. i want “transparent about what we know / don’t know” without sounding vague.

Wei Chen: i’m looking at the “Investigating” blocks. some of the phrases feel like we’re asserting impact before we’ve validated. example: “Customers are unable to access Hosted API in us-east.” — that’s too strong if we only have internal alerts.

Christine Wong: agreed. on-call will often only know “elevated 5xx at gateway” + some reports. we need a safe default that’s still useful.

Elliot Price: from docs POV: keep it consistent with the new public guidance. the status page is customer-facing; avoid internal terms like “burn rate” / “SLO breach” / “scheduler”.

Paula Mendes: ok, proposal for Investigating template:

Option A:
“Investigating: We’re investigating reports of elevated errors and/or latency affecting {capability} in {region}. We’ll share an update within {X} minutes.”

Option B:
“Investigating: We’re aware of an issue impacting {capability} in {region}. We’re investigating and will provide updates as we learn more.”

Thoughts?

Michael Grant: prefer A’s “reports of” + “elevated errors/latency” vs “aware of an issue impacting” (B reads like confirmed impact). also be careful with promising an update in X minutes unless we can meet it consistently.

Talia Benson: +1. we can align with the project metric (TTFU) internally but the template probably shouldn’t commit to a specific minute count.

Marissa Cole: can we add a sentence on scope uncertainty? like “Impact appears limited to a subset of requests” *if we have signals*.

Wei Chen: i’d gate that behind a bracketed clause: “If confirmed: Impact appears to affect a subset of requests.” Otherwise we’ll end up using it as a default and get yelled at.

Christine Wong: + we should define when we’re allowed to say “subset” vs “widespread.” i’ve seen it used to soften language even when it’s basically all traffic.

Paula Mendes: what if Investigating is:
“Investigating: We’re investigating elevated error rates for {capability} in {region}. Some customers may see failures or timeouts. We’ll share updates as we learn more.”

Michael Grant: “Some customers may see…” is good. avoids asserting universal impact.

Elliot Price: +1. also “failures or timeouts” is plain language. avoid “5xx”.

Kira Thompson: reminder for Dedicated/Private: we should not imply multi-tenant blast radius. template should work when incident is isolated to Hosted only. maybe add {product_surface} token (Hosted API / Console / etc).

Marissa Cole: yes please. Console team also wants incidents to say if Console is impacted vs inference. customers confuse them.

Wei Chen: can we standardize the first clause to always include product surface + region + capability?
Example:
“Investigating: We’re investigating elevated errors affecting Redwood Hosted API — Streaming (us-east).”

Paula Mendes: ok but is that too long on mobile?

Marissa Cole: statuspage truncates after ~80 chars in some views. title line should be concise; details in body.

Christine Wong: +1. keep a short subject line and then 2–3 sentences max.

Paula Mendes: working draft:
Title (status incident title): “Degraded performance: Hosted API Streaming (us-east)”
Investigating body:
“Investigating: We’re investigating elevated errors affecting Streaming requests in us-east. Some customers may see failures or timeouts. We’ll provide updates as we learn more.”

Wei Chen: tweak: remove “requests” twice.
“Investigating: We’re investigating elevated errors affecting Streaming in us-east. Some customers may see failures or timeouts…”

Elliot Price: also “provide updates as we learn more” is fine. we might want a softer reassurance line: “We’re actively working to restore normal service.”

Michael Grant: careful with “restore” if we’re not sure it’s degraded. but in context it’s okay if we’ve opened an incident.

Christine Wong: if we’re posting publicly, we’ve usually confirmed *something* is off. so “working to return service to normal” is ok.

Paula Mendes: ok.

Marissa Cole: Identified template next. current draft says: “Identified: Root cause identified and a fix has been deployed.” That’s doing too much in one state.

Wei Chen: totally. “Identified” should be “we believe we know the cause” + “we’re working on mitigation.” deployment should be “Mitigating” or “Monitoring”.

Christine Wong: + on-call often sets Identified when we know “upstream provider issue” or “bad config rollout” but no fix yet.

Paula Mendes: updated Identified body:
“Identified: We’ve identified the cause of elevated errors affecting {surface}/{capability} in {region}. We’re working on mitigation and will share the next update when available.”

Michael Grant: looks good. do not name third-party vendors unless already public policy. avoid “customer-specific capacity constraints.”

Kira Thompson: for Dedicated/Private guidance: don’t say “multiple customers.” say “an issue” and keep it scoped to the declared components.

Elliot Price: also avoid “data loss” unless confirmed. we can add a standard line for “no evidence of data loss” but only if verified.

Wei Chen: suggest we explicitly *avoid* that line in the default template. it’s tempting and risky.

Marissa Cole: +1. if we need it, it can be a recommended add-on clause after verification.

Paula Mendes: Mitigating template: do we want to mention fallback/traffic shift? like “We’ve applied mitigations including traffic shifting and increased capacity.”

Christine Wong: yes but keep generic. “Traffic shifting” is fine. don’t say which region/provider. also don’t mention “GPU shortage.”

Michael Grant: agreed. “increased capacity” can be ok but avoid implying commitments beyond now.

Wei Chen: proposed Mitigating body:
“Mitigating: We’ve applied mitigations to reduce errors and are monitoring recovery. Some customers may continue to see failures while changes roll out.”

Marissa Cole: love that last clause. sets expectations.

Paula Mendes: Monitoring template: “We’re seeing recovery and are monitoring to ensure stability.” ok?

Christine Wong: add “We’ll update again if conditions change.” helps.

Elliot Price: Resolved template: include impact window + brief summary sentence. but keep it non-technical.

Paula Mendes: ok, last question: do we say “partial outage” vs “degraded performance” early? design wants consistent labels.

Wei Chen: my preference: default to “degraded performance” unless we have strong evidence of widespread unavailability. “partial outage” is confusing anyway.

Christine Wong: +1. and we can use component status (Degraded vs Partial Outage) based on signals; copy should not fight the status label.

Michael Grant: from a comms risk standpoint, “degraded performance” is safer early. just make sure the body explains what customers might see.

Talia Benson: action items:
- Paula to update DES-245 copy blocks with these edits
- Elliot to sanity-check against docs tone guide
- Michael to do quick legal pass on the “Identified/Mitigating” phrasing
Target: EOD tomorrow so we can include in the enablement training deck.

Paula Mendes: :thumbsup: will push v3 in the doc in ~1hr and tag y’all.

Marissa Cole: thanks all. once we settle, i’ll mirror the same strings in the Console “incident detail” view so it doesn’t drift.

Wei Chen: please also add the “don’t promise exact next update time” note to the template guidance. ppl keep adding “next update in 30m” and then miss it.

Paula Mendes: yep adding a guideline note: “Avoid committing to exact update intervals; prioritize accuracy. If you include an ETA, confirm Comms Lead can meet it.”

Christine Wong: (reactions: :thumbsup: x4)
